advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add drift tests that mutate the SOURCE (or drive build_surface for real) so a changed class base/field/method and a changed pinned constant each produce a CHANGED line — not just a callable's params list.
evidence: scripts/gen_api_surface.py docstring: 'a changed class shape (bases, dataclass fields, public-method signatures), or a changed public constant'

tests/unit/test_api_surface_gate.py:129-132 mutates only `surface["rebar.signing"]["sign_manifest"]["params"]` (a callable), never a class descriptor's `bases`/`fields`/`methods` nor a value descriptor's `value`

tests/unit/test_api_surface_gate.py:103 `monkeypatch.setattr(gen, "build_surface", _drifted)` — drift is injected into the returned dict, so introspection (_describe_class/_value_repr) is never on the tested path

tests/unit/test_api_surface_gate.py:141-144 test_no_drift_reported_against_self compares a surface to itself (trivially equal); the committed-baseline subprocess check (line 73-76) compares baseline-vs-live where the baseline was generated by the same descriptor code, so neither can catch a broken descriptor-builder
ABSENCE: search for `_describe` and `_value_repr` in the test file returns no matches — no direct assertion on class/constant descriptor output
advisory.finding: The class-shape and constant-value drift-detection paths the generator docstring claims are guarded are never exercised end-to-end: the RED→GREEN tests monkeypatch build_surface to return a hand-mutated dict, so only diff_surface's generic dict-inequality and main()'s exit code are proven. No test drives _describe_class (bases/fields/methods) or _value_repr against a real changed class or constant, so a regression that made _describe_class stop capturing __bases__ or _value_repr misrepresent a constant would leave the gate silently blind while every test stays green.
scenarios: A behavior-preserving-looking refactor of _describe_class drops the `bases` key or narrows the MRO walk: a real base-class change to RebarError/ConcurrencyError would no longer produce drift and the gate would pass
A refactor of _value_repr stops sorting/formatting a frozenset constant such that a genuine change to KNOWN_ERROR_CODES or FRONT_MATTER_KEYS no longer registers as CHANGED
advisory.suggested_fix: Add tests that construct a real class/constant descriptor via gen._describe / gen._describe_class / gen._value_repr and assert its captured shape (bases, fields, method params, value), plus a RED→GREEN case where a class base or a constant value changes drives a `~ CHANGED` line, so a broken descriptor-builder fails a test.

evidence: scripts/gen_api_surface.py:104: `default = "<none>" if param.default is inspect.Parameter.empty else repr(param.default)`
No sanitisation of address-bearing reprs; search_files for `0x` in tests/unit/api_surface_baseline.json returned no matches (latent today, not yet triggered)
advisory.finding: Function/method parameter defaults are pinned via `repr(param.default)`, which is non-deterministic for defaults whose repr embeds a memory address or a per-process sentinel; such a default would produce spurious 'CHANGED' drift the gate cannot distinguish from a real signature change.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Either capture a deterministic value for non-pinned constant types (dict/list/set/bytes) or record them as an explicit 'unpinned' kind, and soften the docstring/test claim that the gate catches 'any changed public constant'.
evidence: scripts/gen_api_surface.py:155-157: `if isinstance(obj, _PINNED_VALUE_TYPES): return {...} \n return {"kind": "value", "type": type(obj).__name__, "value": None}`

Docstring overclaim: scripts/gen_api_surface.py:12-13 says the gate fails on '...a changed public constant'; but a dict/list/enum/bytes constant's value is never captured, so mutating its contents (e.g. adding/removing a STEP_REGISTRY entry) yields no diff.
Fail-open litmus: for a non-pinned-type constant the 'no drift' verdict is produced identically whether the value is unchanged or changed — the check cannot distinguish clean from never-captured.
dropped.finding: Public constants whose type is not in _PINNED_VALUE_TYPES (dict, list, set, bytes, enum, Path, etc.) are pinned with value:null, so a change to their VALUE produces no drift — contradicting the documented claim that the gate fails on any changed public constant. The committed baseline shows STEP_REGISTRY (a dict) recorded as value:null.
dropped.suggested_fix: In _describe, for a non-pinned type either serialise a deterministic representation (e.g. sorted keys for dict, sorted items for set) or emit kind:'unpinned' so the baseline is honest that the value is not guarded; update the module and test docstrings accordingly.

evidence: scripts/gen_api_surface.py:78-79: the __all__ branch of public_names returns every name verbatim without the inspect.ismodule filter used in the else-branch (lines 85-86), so submodules in __all__ pass through to _describe and land on the module fallback.
dropped.finding: A submodule re-exported through a module's __all__ (e.g. `config` in rebar.__all__) is described as kind:value/type:module/value:null, so only its name is guarded — the submodule's own public surface is entirely unguarded, and this is not among the pinned MODULES.
